messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Definitions alignment: Commit vs Near-Commit vs Pipeline — one-pager + labs

Team —

Quick note: we're still seeing inconsistent mappings of opportunities into Commit / Best Case / Pipeline across AE territories. That variance is skewing our weekly forecasts and makes it hard for Finance to model burn against committed revenue.

I attached a one-pager that I drafted with a suggested minimum rule set (definitions-onepager.pdf). The ask: please review and sign off so we can roll a short training to AEs next week. Key highlights:
- "Commit" = legal/PO signed or verbal exec confirmation + finance/ops acceptance (experience threshold: procurement queued)
- "Near-Commit" (new label proposed) = strong exec buy-in, internal procurement started, close probability 70-85% (use for AE visibility only; excluded from booked commits)
- "Pipeline" = active opportunities earlier than Near-Commit; still in discovery/validation (probability <70%)

Proposed cadence: 30-minute drop-in labs (two slots) + 1-hour manager calibration session. Please reply with preferred lab times below and any immediate objections to the rules.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: definitions-onepager.pdf

Subject: Re: Definitions alignment: Commit vs Near-Commit vs Pipeline — one-pager + labs

+1 on the one-pager, looks clear. A couple of practical notes from AE checks:
- Several reps conflate "Best Case" with "Near-Commit" (they're using Best Case as an internal optimistic projection). If we add "Near-Commit" we should explicitly map what gets pushed into Best Case versus Commit in SFDC.
- Request: include a tiny checklist (3–4 items) reps can use before they flip a deal to Commit. That avoids the back-and-forth we see in weekly commit reviews.

For labs: I can run a noon slot on Tuesday (12:00–12:30 PT) and an afternoon slot Wednesday (15:30–16:00 PT). Manager calibration: Thursday 09:00–10:00 PT works for me.

On the attachment: the "procurement queued" language is helpful but we should add a short example (e.g., "SOW sent and procurement POC assigned").

Monica

Thanks — adding some operational rules that we should bake into the automation layer (and I've attached a quick sample report that flags mismatches): sample_sql_report.csv

Suggested rules (draft):
- Auto-flag to Ops if an opportunity is moved to Commit without a linked PO/SOW or without an "exec verbal" field filled by the AE.
- Best Case should be used strictly as a rolling 90-day optimistic view; do not promote to Commit without procurement evidence.
- Near-Commit: AE should fill out a 2-field form ("Decision maker confirmed" + "Procurement engagement status") before pipeline owner can approve.

If we agree, I can add these checks to the weekly sync and wire alerts into the AE dashboard so managers see mismatches ahead of commit reviews. Also: linking the doc here — https://docs.google.com/document/d/definitions-onepager

Karthik
